[+(b) The commissioner must invite talent scouts or coaches from all of Minnesota's professional and college soccer teams, regardless of division level. The commissioner may invite talent scouts or coaches from additional professional and college teams. +]

[+(1) participation rates; +]

[+(3) success stories, including scholarships awarded and players advancing to higher levels of competition; and +]

[+(e) The commissioner must communicate with the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, the United States Soccer Federation, and international soccer organizations, including but not limited to the Premier League and Bundesliga, to develop further opportunities for youth soccer participation and global exposure of the African Youth Soccer League. +]

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to children, youth, and families; establishing an African Youth Soccer League; requiring reports; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. AFRICAN YOUTH SOCCER LEAGUE.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

The commissioner of children, youth, and families must establish an African Youth Soccer League to ensure access to resources, facilities, and development programs for young soccer players of African descent.

Subd. 2.

Local partnerships.

The commissioner must partner with local schools, community centers, cities, and semiprofessional and professional soccer clubs to provide access to high-quality training facilities and soccer fields for practices and games.

Subd. 3.

Coaching licenses.

The commissioner must provide an opportunity and funding for coaches within the African Youth Soccer League to obtain coaching licenses through the United States Soccer Federation.

Subd. 4.

Mental health.

The commissioner of children, youth, and families, in collaboration with the commissioner of human services, must provide access to mental health services for youth soccer players within the African Youth Soccer League.

Subd. 5.

Annual showcase.

(a) Each summer, the commissioner must host an annual showcase tournament for the African Youth Soccer League.

(b) The commissioner must invite talent scouts or coaches from all of Minnesota's professional and college soccer teams, regardless of division level. The commissioner may invite talent scouts or coaches from additional professional and college teams.

Subd. 6.

Report.

The commissioner must submit an annual report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over children, youth, and families that provides the following details about the African Youth Soccer League:

(1) participation rates;

(2) financial expenditures and funding allocations;

(3) success stories, including scholarships awarded and players advancing to higher levels of competition; and

(4) the impact of soccer on mental health and overall community engagement.

Sec. 2. DIRECTION TO THE COMMISSIONER OF CHILDREN, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES; AFRICAN YOUTH SOCCER LEAGUE DEVELOPMENT.

(a) The commissioner of children, youth, and families must develop a grant program that provides financial assistance for community-based soccer teams within the African Youth Soccer League to acquire uniforms, soccer balls, and other necessary equipment.

(b) The commissioner must develop a mentorship program that would pair youth soccer players from the African Youth Soccer League with professional and semiprofessional soccer players.

(c) The commissioner must develop a grant program that provides grants to youth soccer players within the African Youth Soccer League to help the players access higher education and professional development programs.

(d) The commissioner, in collaboration with the commissioner of public safety, must develop programs that engage at-risk youth in soccer activities within the African Youth Soccer League.

(e) The commissioner must communicate with the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, the United States Soccer Federation, and international soccer organizations, including but not limited to the Premier League and Bundesliga, to develop further opportunities for youth soccer participation and global exposure of the African Youth Soccer League.

Sec. 3. APPROPRIATION; AFRICAN YOUTH SOCCER LEAGUE.

$3,700,000 in fiscal year 2026 and $3,700,000 in fiscal year 2027 are appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of children, youth, and families to establish and oversee the African Youth Soccer League.
